messages.subject: Re-scaling / transforming factor loadings
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to replicate the CFA for ipsative items as suggested by Cheung & Chan (2002). Their model imposes a 'rescaling parameter' on the factor loadings (see p. 66). In the proposed model, each factor loading is 'rescaled' by subtracting the average value for all factor loadings. Roughly reproducing their proposal, a one-factor model with three observed indicators such as

factor1 =~ load1*x1 + load2*x2 + load3*x3

would be transformed to

factor1 =~ tran1*x1 + tran2*x2 + tran3*x3

where
tran1 = load1 - ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)
tran2 = load2 - ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)
tran3 = load3 - ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)


I wonder how this transformation of factor loadings could be implemented in lavaan. (Other proposed transformations seem to be more easily implemented in lavaan.)

Thanks!


Mike W.-L. Cheung & Wai Chan (2002) Reducing Uniform Response Bias With Ipsative Measurement in Multiple-Group Confirmatory Factor Analysis, Structural Equation Modeling, 9:1, 55-77.
https://doi.org/10.1207/S15328007SEM0901_4

parts:
Hi Fabricio,

I do not know this transformation. What I wonder is this:

tran1 = load1 - ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)
tran2 = load2 - ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)
tran3 = load3 - ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)

means

load1 = ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)
load2 = ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)
load3 = ((load1 + load2 + load3)/3)

This should only be the case if load1 = load2 = load3. Right?

Maybe I'm making a big error in reasoning (it's already late in the evening) or the transformation works somehow differently? Or is it an additional parameter calculated based on the estimated loadings (in which case it would be easy)?

Best

Christian

messages.subject: Re: Re-scaling / transforming factor loadings
parts:
Hi Christian,

This transformation has been proposed by Cheung & Chan to address some measurement issues with ipsative data. The transformation/correction basically states that a said loading must be 'corrected' taking the average of all loadings in consideration. E
quality of loadings (e.g., load1 = load2 = load3) is not required.

I just added a print screen of the model proposed by Cheung & Chen for clarification -- I hope there is no copyright issues with that. 

The factor loadings transformation is what I have found challenging to implement. I am unsure about how to define the transformation using lavaan syntax. Cheung & Chan provide EQS syntax in the appendix but I haven' t used EQS in ages so I am unable to convert it into lavaan syntax. 

Best,
Fabricio
